subject: general
question: What determines the atomic number of an element?

options.text: Number of neutrons in an isotope
Number of electrons in all shells
Total number of protons in nucleus

solution:
The correct answer is __**Total number of protons in nucleus**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **atomic number** (represented by the symbol **Z**) of a chemical element is defined as the **total number of protons** found in the **nucleus** of every atom of that element.
 
• It is the fundamental property that determines the **identity** of an element; for example, every atom with **6 protons** is **Carbon**, and every atom with **79 protons** is **Gold**.
 
• The concept was significantly advanced by **Henry Moseley** in **1913**, who used **X-ray spectroscopy** to show that the atomic number is a physical property linked to the **nuclear charge**.
 
• In the **Modern Periodic Table**, elements are arranged in increasing order of their **atomic numbers**, as per the **Modern Periodic Law**.
 
• While the number of **electrons** can change (forming **ions**) and the number of **neutrons** can vary (forming **isotopes**), the **number of protons** remains constant for a specific element. ***Hence, the correct answer is Total number of protons in nucleus.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Mass Number (A):**
 
 
• This is the sum of the total number of **protons** and **neutrons** present in the nucleus of an atom. These particles are collectively known as **nucleons**.
 
• The formula is expressed as **A = Z + N**, where **N** is the number of **neutrons**.
 
 
 
• **Isotopes:**
 
 
• These are atoms of the **same element** that possess the same **atomic number** but different **mass numbers** due to a varying number of **neutrons**.
 
• For example, **Hydrogen** has three isotopes: **Protium** (0 neutrons), **Deuterium** (1 neutron), and **Tritium** (2 neutrons).
 
 
 
• **Electrons and Ions:**
 
 
• In a **neutral atom**, the number of **electrons** is equal to the **atomic number** (protons).
 
• When an atom gains or loses electrons, it becomes an **ion** (cation or anion), but its **atomic number** remains **unchanged** because the proton count does not change.
 
 
 
• **Isobars:**
 
 
• These are atoms of **different elements** that have the same **mass number** but different **atomic numbers**. An example is **Calcium** and **Argon**, both having a mass number of **40**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Discovery of Subatomic Particles:**
 
 
• The **Electron** was discovered by **J.J. Thomson** in **1897** through his **cathode ray tube** experiment.
 
• The **Proton** was effectively discovered following **Ernest Rutherford's** **gold foil experiment** in **1911**, which identified the **atomic nucleus**.
 
• The **Neutron** was discovered by **James Chadwick** in **1932**, explaining the additional mass in the nucleus that protons could not account for alone.
 
 
 
• **Chemical Properties:**
 
 
• The **atomic number** determines the **electronic configuration** of an atom, which in turn determines its **chemical behavior** and reactivity.
 
• The number of **valence electrons** (electrons in the outermost shell) is what primarily dictates how an element bonds with others.
